transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi Doc, thanks for seeing me. I, uh... I hope I'm not wasting your time. I'm sure you see folks with much bigger problems. But, well, what finally got me to come in is that over these past few months, my mind just keeps... jumping around. 

I drive a truck for a living, and I'm usually really on top of things, I promise. But lately, every little CB chirp, or a fuel price sign on the highway, or just some random new idea I get... it completely grabs my attention. And because of that, I've been missing some small details I normally never miss. Nothing terrible! Just, you know, overlooking a client's delivery note, or forgetting who I promised to call back. 

I just want to make sure I'm doing my job right and keeping my clients happy, you know? Does that... does that make sense to be here for?
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, energized, or wired compared with your normal self?

Well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm bouncing off the walls or anything crazy like that. But, um, yeah, for months now I've had these stretches where I'm just really fired up. Like, I'll wake up feeling like everything is just going to work out perfectly, no matter what. It's a good feeling, honestly! I get a lot done. 

But... well, I guess there's a flip side to it, too. I hate to admit it, but sometimes instead of feeling good, I just feel... edgy. Like I'm snapping over little things at home or when I'm working in the yard. Things that normally wouldn't bother me at all. I really try to keep a lid on it, because that's not the kind of guy I am, you know? I don't like being short with my family. 

Is it normal to flip-flop like that? Being super positive and then just... cranky? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
During these fired-up periods, do you need less sleep than usual?

Well, I mean... I wouldn't say I *need* less sleep, exactly. I know how important rest is, especially driving for a living. I always aim for a full night! 

But, uh, I guess lately, when I'm feeling that kind of... energized way... I have been waking up pretty early. Like, I'll maybe get three or four hours of sleep, and then I'm just up. Before the sun's even out. And the funny thing is, I don't feel worn out at all. I actually feel totally ready to roll, you know? Ready to tackle the day. 

I hope that doesn't sound irresponsible. I really do try to stay in bed and rest, but my body just tells me it's time to get going. Is that... is that okay? I mean, as long as I'm not tired behind the wheel, right?
When you feel that fired-up way, do you find yourself taking on a lot more projects or staying unusually busy than is normal for you?

Well, I suppose I do stay pretty busy. I mean, I like to be helpful, you know? I don't want you to think I'm running myself into the ground or anything. I just... I like getting things done. 

But, um, yeah, when I'm feeling like that, I do tend to find extra jobs for myself. Like, I'll spend my evenings rewriting all my route plans to make them more efficient, or I'll stay late to check in on the new drivers, just to make sure they're doing okay. And then I'll get home and start fixing things around the house that have been on the list for ages. 

I just... I get this feeling like I can't really sit still. If I sit on the couch for too long, I just feel kind of antsy, like I should be doing something productive. I figure it's better to be a hard worker than lazy, right? I hope that's not a bad thing... is it okay to want to stay that busy?
When you’re in those fired-up periods, do you find yourself talking more than usual?

Well, I... I try not to talk people's ears off, you know? I've always thought of myself as a pretty good listener. I wouldn't want to be one of those guys who just dominates the conversation and doesn't let anyone else get a word in edgewise. 

But, I mean, I guess... maybe I do chat a bit more when I'm feeling good like that? Like, I'll be at the depot, and I just feel really friendly, so I'll start talking to the dispatchers or the other drivers, maybe a little more than I normally would. But I always try to keep it positive and friendly! I'm not, like, rambling or anything. 

I don't think it's too much, really. Just being sociable, right? People generally seem to like it when you're upbeat and friendly... I hope I'm not annoying anyone. Do you think that sounds like it's within normal limits?
When you’re in those fired-up periods, do you feel more confident or capable than usual?

Well, I... I definitely try to stay humble. I know I'm just a driver, and I respect the management team a lot. I really wouldn't want to come across as arrogant or like I think I know better than everyone else. 

But, um... I guess when I'm feeling really energized like that, I do feel pretty good about what I can handle. Like, I actually got it in my head recently that I could completely rebuild our whole driver training program. I just felt so sure that I could make it run smoother and better than how the bosses have it set up. 

I mean, I know that's not really my lane, and I shouldn't be stepping on toes. I just wanted to help the company, you know? Because I felt like I had all these great ideas and the energy to pull it off. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm getting a big head or being disrespectful to my supervisors. It's good to take initiative at work, right? As long as I mean well?
During those fired-up periods, have you ever felt like you had special abilities or powers that other people don’t have?

Oh, goodness no. I mean, I definitely wouldn't want you to think I was losing touch with reality or anything like that. I'm just a regular guy, you know? I drive a truck, I do my job, and I try to be a good neighbor. 

I've never thought I could fly or read minds or anything crazy like that. I just... I just feel really capable sometimes, like we talked about with the training program. But I know my limits. I know I'm just a regular person. 

I try to keep my feet firmly on the ground, you know? I wouldn't want anyone to think I was acting strange or making things up. That would be pretty concerning, wouldn't it? I hope it's clear that I'm just talking about feeling productive and having good ideas, nothing out of the ordinary.
During those fired-up periods, do you do things that are unusually risky or impulsive for you?

Well, I really try to be responsible, you know? Being a driver, safety is the number one thing. I take my job very seriously, and I would never want to do anything that would put myself or anyone else in danger, or make the company look bad. I pride myself on having a clean driving record.

So, no, I don't think I do anything crazy or reckless. I mean, maybe when I'm feeling really good, I might, I don't know, treat myself a little more? Like, maybe stop for a nicer lunch on the road instead of packing a sandwich, or maybe buy a round of coffees for the guys at the depot. But nothing out of control. 

I definitely don't go blowing my savings or doing anything dangerous. I'm a pretty cautious guy by nature. I hope that's what you're asking? I just try to be a good, reliable person, even when I've got all that extra energy. That's the right way to handle it, don't you think?
During those fired-up times, do your thoughts race from one idea to another?

Well, um... I try to keep a pretty clear head, to be honest. You know, when you're driving for a living, you really have to stay focused on the road. You can't afford to have your mind just... bouncing all over the place. 

So, even when I'm having one of those really energized weeks, I feel like my thoughts are actually... well, pretty organized. I mean, maybe I'm just thinking a little sharper than usual, but they definitely don't race out of control or get all jumbled up. 

I really wouldn't want you to think I'm scatterbrained or can't concentrate on my job. I always make sure to stay on task and think things through. That's a good sign, right? Being able to keep my thoughts in order like that?
During those fired-up periods, does your behavior ever cause problems at work or at home?

Well, I... I wouldn't really call them problems, exactly. I mean, I always want to do a good job, and I really try to be the best husband and provider I can be. I'd hate for you to think I was dropping the ball. 

But, um... I guess there have been a few little hiccups. Like at work, I've... well, I've had to ask dispatch, and maybe a couple of clients, to repeat some details that I really should have kept track of. And a couple of my sales follow-ups kind of slipped through the cracks. Not because I don't care about the work! Just... I was chasing a few too many ideas at once, trying to be really productive, you know? I hope my boss knows my intentions are good. 

And, uh, at home... I hate to admit this because I really want to be the one helping out, but... I can tell my wife and my daughter have been sort of walking on eggshells around me. I think I'm adding a little bit of strain when I'm supposed to be the one supporting them. It makes me feel pretty bad to say that out loud, to be honest. But it's nothing we can't work through, right? Every family has little bumps in the road like that, don't you think?
Before these past few months, did you have similar problems with distractibility and feeling unusually energized earlier in life, like back in childhood or your teens?

Well, gosh, thinking back that far... I really don't think so. I mean, I was always a pretty good kid, you know? I tried hard in school, even if it wasn't my favorite thing, and I always respected my parents and my teachers. I'd never want to be one of those kids who was bouncing off the walls or causing trouble in class. 

So, no, I don't remember ever feeling like this back then. I was just a regular teenager, maybe a little energetic sometimes, like playing sports or hanging out with friends, but definitely nothing unusual or... or distracting. I always tried to do what was expected of me. That's normal for a kid growing up, right? Just having regular energy and trying to be good?
When you get into one of these fired-up periods, does it last for at least 4 days in a row?

Well, um... I really try not to let things drag on, you know? I like to get back to my normal routine as quickly as possible. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm just out there running wild for days on end. 

But, I guess... if I'm being completely honest, when I get that really big burst of energy, it does stick around for a little while. Maybe... maybe four or five days? Sometimes a whole work week. But I always try to keep a lid on it and just use it to get more stops done on my route. It's not like I'm out of control for that whole time, just... running a little hotter than usual. That's not too bad, is it? Just a few days of being extra productive?
Have you had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day?

Well, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, you know? I think it's important to be a cheerful guy, especially for my family and the customers on my route. I'd never want to be a burden or bring everyone else down by moping around for weeks on end. 

Sure, everybody has a bad day here and there, maybe feels a little tired after a long shift, but... two whole weeks of just feeling down and not caring about anything? No, sir. I always make sure to get up, go to work, and take care of my responsibilities. I try to be dependable like that. That's the right way to handle things, isn't it? Just keeping your chin up and pushing through?
Have you ever been hospitalized because of one of these fired-up periods?

Oh, goodness, no. Hospitalized? No, I've never had anything like that happen. I mean, I would never let things get so out of hand that I'd need to be in a hospital. I always make sure I'm taking care of myself and staying out of trouble, you know? 

Like I said, when I get that extra energy, I just put it into my work. I'd never want to cause a scene or make my family worry to the point where they'd think I needed to be locked up somewhere. I'm a responsible guy, I promise. It's just a little extra pep in my step sometimes, nothing that requires a doctor or a hospital bed. That shows I'm handling it okay, right? If I've never had to go to the hospital for it?
